{{Short description|American mathematician}}
[[File:Robert Bixby.jpg|thumb|right|Robert E. Bixby]]
'''Robert E. Bixby''' is an American mathematician, the Noah Harding Professor Emeritus of Computational and Applied Mathematics at [[Rice University]]. 

Bixby received a [[Bachelor of Science]] with a major in [[industrial engineering]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] (1968) and a [[Doctor of Philosophy]] in [[operations research]] from [[Cornell University]] (1972).<ref>{{Cite web |title=Robert Bixby {{!}} Faculty {{!}} The People of Rice {{!}} Rice University |url=https://profiles.rice.edu/faculty/robert-bixby |access-date=2023-04-08 |website=profiles.rice.edu}}</ref> His dissertation, ''Composition and Decomposition of Matroids and Related Topics'', concerned [[matroid theory]] and was supervised by [[Louis Billera]]. His doctoral students have included [[Collette Coullard]] at [[Northwestern University]], and [[Eva K. Lee]] at Rice.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=14993}}</ref>

He is the President and Co-founder of Gurobi Optimization.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Rothberg |first1=Edward |title=Gurobi Optimization |url=https://www.informs.org/Impact/O.R.-Analytics-Success-Stories/Industry-Profiles/Gurobi-Optimization |website=O.R. & Analytics Success Stories |publisher=[[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences|INFORMS]] |access-date=21 May 2023}}</ref> In 1987 he co-founded [[CPLEX]] Optimization, which was acquired by [[ILOG]] in 1997. 

Bixby was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1997 for contributions to [[combinatorial optimization]] and the development and commercialization of high-performance optimization software.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://ga.rice.edu/emeritusfaculty/ |title=Emeritus Faculty |publisher=rice.edu |accessdate=December 13, 2016 |archive-date=August 5, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170805174149/http://ga.rice.edu/emeritusfaculty/ |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://ieor.berkeley.edu/people/advisory/profiles/bixby |title=Robert E. Bixby |publisher=berkeley.edu |accessdate=December 13, 2016 |archive-date=September 1, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170901013939/http://ieor.berkeley.edu/people/advisory/profiles/bixby |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.worldcat.org/identities/lccn-n78017318/ |title=Bixby, Robert E. |publisher=worldcat.org |accessdate=December 13, 2016}}</ref> He is also a fellow of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/Fellows-Alphabetical-List|title=Fellows: Alphabetical List|publisher=[[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]]|accessdate=2019-10-09}}</ref>
